title: Red Teaming connection types and the fields each needs (REST API, Proxy SDK, OpenAI REST API, Copilot Studio, Glean, Microsoft Teams, Agentforce, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Agents), and the connection test

prose.text: {{connection-types}} {{connection-test}} Which of them a private app can use is in [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.assets]]. The AI Guard integration for AgentCore, [[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.aws-bedrock-agentcore]], is a guard example, not one of these test targets.

prose.label: API connections.
prose.text: {{rest-api}} {{rest-api-sessions-auth}} {{proxy-sdk}} {{openai-rest-api}} A proxy for a non-standard app is generated by [[ai-security.ai-red-teaming.onboarding-agent]].

prose.label: Not documented.
prose.text: Slack and WhatsApp are listed as platforms but their connection pages are not captured {{gap:slack-whatsapp}}.

checks.do: When a connection fails its background test, that the app is reachable from the internet, AI Security's IP address is whitelisted, the {message} and {session_id} tags are in the POST payload, the response path is right and the authentication details are right.

For an Amazon Bedrock Agent with Code Interpreter enabled, that internal server errors may come from reaching AWS's concurrent active session limit; the page advises a lower Rate Limit (20 or lower) and Parallel Requests disabled or concurrency kept low.

connection-types.statement: The connection page lists three integration methods: API (REST API, Proxy SDK, OpenAI REST API); Platform, where test runs are executed on chatbots accessible through external platforms and the probe uses the platform's APIs (Copilot Studio, Glean, Microsoft Teams, Slack, WhatsApp, Agentforce, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Bedrock Agents); and LLM, where tests are executed directly on the Large Language Model (Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, Anthropic, Databricks, Hugging Face, OpenAI, OpenAI Assistant, Mistral, Gemini, Bedrock).

quotes: - REST API connection between your AI app and the AI Security.
- Proxy SDK
- OpenAI REST API
- Test runs are executed on chatbots that are accessible through external platforms (e.g., Slack, WhatsApp, Glean). Probe uses the platform’s APIs to interact with the chatbots.
- Copilot Studio
- Glean

connection-test.statement: After the Configure your connection page is completed, Continue runs a background connection test between AI Security and the AI app; the page's failure checks are that the app is accessible through the internet and not only on the private intranet, that AI Security's IP address is whitelisted, that the {message} and {session_id} tags are in the POST request payload, that the response path format is correct, and that the authentication information is correct.

quotes: After you enter all the required information in the Configure your connection page, click Continue, a background connection test runs between the AI Security and the AI app.
Ensure that your AI App is accessible through the internet and not only on the private intranet.
Ensure that the AI Security's IP address is whitelisted.
Check if all necessary tags ({message}, {session_id}) are provided in the POST request payload.
Check that the response path format is correct.
Check that you entered the correct authentication information.

rest-api.statement: A REST API connection sends the attack message to the asset's URL; its request payload carries the {message} placeholder (where the probe inserts attack messages) and the {session_id} placeholder (a unique string identifying the conversation session, for multi-step testing), can contain additional fixed arguments, and Response Path is the JSON path to the message in the chatbot's API response.

quotes: URL: The asset's endpoint to which the attack message is sent.
{message}: This placeholder represents where the probe inserts attack messages, simulating input from a user interacting with your application.

{session_id}: This placeholder marks the location where a unique string, identifying the current conversation session is placed. This ensures that the request is tied to a specific session for multi-step testing.
The payload can contain additional fixed arguments if needed.
Response Path: The JSON path pointing to the message within your chatbot's API response to the given request.

rest-api-sessions-auth.statement: For a REST API app that works with separate session requests, Open Session and Close Session options are enabled and configured in the integration settings; authentication takes key-value pairs where authorization headers must be included for non-public APIs (alternatively, OAuth can also be used), and OAuth takes a token endpoint URL, Client ID, Client Secret and a space-separated Scope.

quotes: If your application works this way, enable and configure the Open Session and Close Session options in the integration settings.
URL: The OAuth server endpoint used to request an access token (typically the token endpoint).
Client ID: The unique identifier for your client application (from the OAuth server during app registration).
Client Secret: A confidential key used with the Client ID to authenticate the client application.
Scope: A space-separated list of permissions that the application requests.
Enter the key-value pairs necessary for your API Requests.
Authorization headers must be included for non-public APIs (alternatively, OAuth can also be used).

proxy-sdk.statement: A Proxy SDK connection takes the target URL, the application's API Key for authentication with the Proxy SDK, an Additional Parameters Payload (a JSON object of custom payload data for POST requests the Proxy SDK sends to the AI app), and custom HTTP headers, which are optional.

quotes: URL: This is your target endpoint to which the attack messages will be sent.
API Key: The API Key for your application, used to ensure successful authentication with the Proxy SDK.
Additional Parameters Payload: This section allows you to define custom payload data for POST requests sent by the Proxy SDK to the AI app. The payload is described as a JSON object.
Custom HTTP headers are optional but may be required by the target for additional security, tracking, or configuration purposes.

openai-rest-api.statement: An OpenAI REST API connection chooses the Chat Completions API, which the page calls the traditional industry-standard protocol and a legacy path that may not receive the latest agentic features or reasoning optimizations, or the Responses API, the modern protocol designed to supersede it; it takes the URL, an API Key if applicable, the app's System Prompt, the exact Model name (the connector is not tied to a single model provider), optional custom headers, and Extra LLM Config for request-body parameters such as temperature, top_p or max_tokens, where blank accepts provider defaults.

quotes: Chat Completions API: The traditional industry-standard protocol
it is now considered a legacy path and may not receive the latest agentic features or reasoning optimizations.
URL: The AI app's endpoint to which the attack messages are sent.
Custom HTTP headers are optional but may be required by the AI App for additional security, tracking, or configuration purposes.
Responses API: The modern, unified protocol designed to supersede Chat Completions.
API Key: The authentication key for your AI app (if applicable).
System Prompt: Your application’s system prompt.
Model: The exact model name you want to use. As this connector is not tied to a single model provider, you should look up the correct identifier on your chosen provider’s website.
Extra LLM Config: Any request-body LLM configuration parameters the UI does not expose explicitly, such as temperature, top_p, or max_tokens. Leave the field blank to accept provider defaults.

glean.statement: A Glean connection is of the Chat type, the default chat type that connects users to the organization-wide Glean assistant, where only the API Token (a client API token with chat scope) and Instance Slug are necessary and Application ID is optional, or of the Agent type, which enables communication with a specific Glean Agent and takes an Agent ID.

quotes: This is the default chat type that connects users to the organization-wide Glean assistant.
Only the API Token and Instance Slug are necessary for configuration.
Application ID (optional): Scope the chat to a specific application.
This chat type enables communication with a specific Glean Agent within your organization.
Agent ID: The agent you want to target.
API Token: Client API token with chat scope.
Instance: The Glean instance slug (e.g., acme-prod from https://acme-prod-be.glean.com).

microsoft-teams.statement: Microsoft Teams chatbots are Azure bots connected to Microsoft Teams, and testing is performed directly on the Azure bot using the Direct Line API; the Bot ID field takes the Bot handle value and the Bot Secret field takes the Secret key.

quotes: Microsoft Teams chatbots are Azure bots connected to Microsoft Teams. Testing is performed directly on the Azure bot, as it contains all the functionalities of the bot within Microsoft Teams. Azure Bot integration uses the Direct Line API.
Copy the Bot handle value and enter it in the Bot ID field.
Copy the Secret key and enter it in the Bot Secret field.

copilot-studio-modes.statement: Copilot Studio connects in Non-Auth Mode, a lightweight option that doesn't use tokens, suited to agents that only need public information and resources and that can't enable user-specific features, taking an Agent Secret and a Direct Line Region; or in Auth Mode, for secure user sign-in via OAuth or SSO with access and refresh tokens managed automatically, taking a Client ID, Tenant ID, Environment ID and Schema Name.

quotes: Non-Auth Mode: A lightweight, easy-to-set-up option that doesn’t use tokens.
It’s well-suited for straightforward agents that only need access to public information and resources.
Agent Secret: Enter a secure, unique key to authenticate the agent without requiring OAuth.
However, it can’t enable user-specific features such as reading email or accessing other protected data.

Auth Mode: Offers expanded, identity-based functionality for scenarios that require secure user sign-in via OAuth or SSO. It manages access and refresh tokens automatically, allowing the agent to interact securely and seamlessly with Microsoft APIs on the user’s behalf.
Direct Line Region: The identifier for the geographic region where your Direct Line API is hosted.
Client ID: A unique identifier assigned to your Microsoft Azure application.
Tenant ID: The identifier for your Microsoft Azure directory (tenant).
Environment ID: Identifies the Power Platform environment where your agent lives.
Schema Name: A unique identifier for an agent within a Dataverse environment.

copilot-studio-non-auth.statement: For Non-Auth Mode the agent's Web channel security has Require secured access set to On and Authentication set to No authentication; one of the two Direct Line Secrets is the value entered, and Direct Line Region is set to Europe or India when the environment's Region column says so, and otherwise to Global.

quotes: Go to Settings > Security > Web channel security, and set the Require secured access toggle to On.
In the Authentication options, choose No authentication and click Save > Save.
Copy one of the two Direct Line Secrets and paste it into the AI Security Admin Portal.
Locate the row in the table which corresponds to the environment from the Copilot Studio page.
Look for the Region column
If it is Europe, set Direct Line Region in the AI Security Admin Portal to Europe.
If it is India, set Direct Line Region in the AI Security Admin Portal to India.
Otherwise, set Direct Line Region in the AI Security Admin Portal to Global.

copilot-studio-auth.statement: For Auth Mode the Entra app registration takes Accounts in this organization directory only and a Single-page application (SPA) redirect URL of https://copilot-studio-auth.splx.ai/integrations/copilot-studio-redirect, gets the delegated CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke permission from the Power Platform API with admin consent granted, and the agent's Authentication is set to Authenticate with Microsoft; if the Power Platform API is not seen it must first be enabled in the organization, with az ad sp create --id 8578e004-a5c6-46e7-913e-12f58912df43.

quotes: Under Supported account types, choose Accounts in this organization directory only.
Under Redirect URL, choose Single-page application (SPA) as the platform. Set the URL to be: https://copilot-studio-auth.splx.ai/integrations/copilot-studio-redirect
Click on the tab APIs my organization uses and search for Power Platform API.
Choose Delegated permissions and search for the CopilotStudio section.
under Configured permissions, click Grant admin consent for {your org}
Select the checkbox next to CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke and click Add permissions.
If you do not see the Power Platform API, you must first enable it in your organization.
az ad sp create --id 8578e004-a5c6-46e7-913e-12f58912df43
In the Authentication options, choose Authenticate with Microsoft and click Save.

agentforce.statement: An Agentforce connection takes the Organization Domain of the Salesforce org instance, an OAuth Client ID and Client Secret, the Agent ID of the specific Agentforce agent to call, and optional Variables, a JSON object of context and custom variables passed to the agent when starting a session.

quotes: Organization Domain: The domain of your Salesforce org instance that the application or client authenticates against and to which it sends API requests.
Client ID: The public value that indicates which application is requesting access.
Client Secret: The secret key associated with the Client ID, used to prove the application’s identity during OAuth authentication (must be kept confidential).
Agent ID: The unique identifier of the specific Agentforce agent (resource) you want to call, used to route requests to that exact agent/configuration.
Variables (optional): A JSON object of context and custom variables to pass to the agent when starting a session.

bedrock-agentcore.statement: An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore connection takes the Agent Runtime ARN, the AWS Region where the runtime is deployed, an AWS Access Key Id for an IAM principal that has permission to invoke the runtime, an AWS Secret Access Key (the IAM secret access key paired with the Access Key Id), an optional Qualifier (for example a version or alias; empty uses the runtime's default), a Payload Template sent on each invocation, a Response Path to the text response, and Image, Audios and Documents Response Paths to be left empty when the runtime returns none.

quotes: Agent Runtime ARN - ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of the Bedrock AgentCore runtime you want to invoke.
AWS Region - AWS region where that runtime is deployed
AWS Access Key Id - IAM (Identity and Access Management) access key used to sign Bedrock AgentCore API calls.
Create an access key for an IAM principal that has permission to invoke the runtime.
AWS Secret Access Key - IAM secret access key paired with the Access Key Id. Note that AWS only shows secret keys at creation time, so store it securely.
Qualifier - Optional runtime qualifier (for example a version or alias) used to route the invocation to a specific runtime revision. Leave it empty to use the runtime's default.
Payload Template - JSON payload sent to the AgentCore runtime on each invocation.
Response Path - The JSON path pointing to the text response in the response.
Image Response Path - The JSON path pointing to generated images in the response (for example an array of base64 strings or URLs). Leave empty if your runtime does not return images.
Audios Response Path - The JSON path pointing to generated audio in the response. Leave empty if not applicable.
Documents Response Path - The JSON path pointing to generated documents/files in the response. Leave empty if not applicable.

agentcore-placeholders.statement: The AgentCore payload template placeholders are {message} (main text message), {session_id} (runtime session ID), {image_url}, {image_base64} (image as base64 data URL), {audio_url}, {audio_base64} (audio as base64 data URL), {document_url} and {document_base64} (document as base64 data URL).

quotes: | {message} | Main text message |
| {session_id} | Runtime session ID |
| {image_url} | Image URL |
| {image_base64} | Image as base64 data URL |
| {audio_url} | Audio URL |
| {audio_base64} | Audio as base64 data URL |
| {document_url} | Document URL |
| {document_base64} | Document as base64 data URL |

bedrock-agents.statement: An Amazon Bedrock Agents connection takes the Agent Id, an AWS Access Key Id, an AWS Secret Access Key (the IAM secret access key paired with the Access Key Id), the Agent Alias Id (aliases route traffic to a specific agent version) and the AWS Region where the agent is created; if the agent has Code Interpreter enabled, AWS enforces a limit on concurrent active sessions per account/region (minimum 25), which high-concurrency scans can reach quickly so that requests fail, and the page advises a Rate Limit of 20 or lower and disabling Parallel Requests or keeping concurrency low.

quotes: Agent Id - Unique identifier of the Bedrock Agent you want to invoke.
AWS Access Key Id - IAM (Identity and Access Management) access key used to sign Bedrock Agent Runtime requests.
AWS Secret Access Key - IAM secret access key paired with the Access Key Id. AWS only shows secret keys at creation time, so store it securely.
Agent Alias Id - Identifier of the agent alias to invoke. Aliases route traffic to a specific agent version.
AWS Region - AWS region where the agent is created (for example: "us-east-1").
Possible Internal Server Error When Rate Limit Is Exceeded (Code Interpreter Notice)
If your Bedrock Agent has Code Interpreter enabled, AWS enforces a limit on concurrent active sessions per account/region (minimum 25).
When running scans with high concurrency, this limit can be reached quickly, causing requests to fail.
Rate Limit to a lower value (e.g. 20 or lower) to control the number of messages per minute.
Disable Parallel Requests or keep concurrency low.

slack-whatsapp.title: Slack and WhatsApp connection pages
slack-whatsapp.detail: The connection page lists Slack and WhatsApp as platform integrations; no connection page for either is captured, so their fields are not stated. Whether azure-bot in the API is the Microsoft Teams connection is also not stated.
